pole_A.claim: Phantasia is the interpretive aspect of perception, 'seeing-as'; broad phainetai-connected scope; pictorial register is peripheral.

pole_B.claim: Phantasia is fundamentally an image-residue / image-faculty: decaying kineseis, pictorial 'places-before-the-eyes,' after-images and dreams central.

debates.notes: Hawhee (PHX-07) explicitly mediates: phantasia 'moves closer to Nussbaum' but is 'grafted onto direct perception' (see PHX-D-006).

pole_A.claim: Phantasia is its own capacity / power of the soul with own causal-explanatory work — not reducible to aisthesis or noesis.

pole_B.claim: Phantasia is NOT a separate faculty but supervenes on / is parasitic upon sense-perception; it performs cognitive functions (synthesis, bridging) without faculty-status.

debates.notes: Caston's response to Frede is the most sustained: 'same in number, different in being' lets one power be SAME-yet-DISTINCT (his appeal to non-Leibnizian identity, fn. 51).

pole_A.claim: Phantasia is a single (or at most binary: calculative/sensitive) faculty across the Aristotelian texts; the apparent diversity (dreams, memory, deliberation) is one phenomenon under varying conditions.

pole_B.claim: Aristotle's account requires THREE kinds of phantasia (calculative / sensitive / indefinite-sub-sensitive), drawing on DA III.11 433b31-434a5 + Themistius/Philoponus/Aquinas; the III.10 433b29 binary is a higher-level dichotomy within a tripartite scheme.

debates.notes: Papachristou's tripartite proposal is the cluster's clearest minority taxonomy.

debates.debate_name: Lexis-narrow vs. epideictic-broad rhetorical home of phantasia

pole_A.claim: Phantasia's rhetorical home is Rhetoric Book III lexis — narrowly construed, often via the Kennedy/Cope reading of 1404a11 as 'outward show.'

pole_B.claim: Phantasia's rhetorical home is broader than lexis: it is anchored in epideictic / amplification (Rhet. I.3, I.9; megethos/auxesis) and in psychological Rhet. II emotion-passages.

debates.notes: Foundational disagreement organizing the cluster's three rhetoric-side authors against the philosophy-side default.

debates.debate_name: Mere-show pejorative vs. legitimate rhetorical function

pole_A.claim: At Rhet. III.1 1404a11 phantasia means 'ostentation / mere show' — Freudenthal 1863's extrapolation, consolidated by Cope, Kennedy, Halliwell; phantasia in rhetoric is pejorative.

pole_B.claim: Phantasia at 1404a11 is the De Anima psychological faculty, not 'mere show': Freudenthal's verb-to-noun extrapolation is unwarranted (noun never elsewhere means 'ostentation' in the 100+ Aristotelian uses); the rhetorical function is legitimate.

debates.notes: González most sustained; Nussbaum's 1978 'kata metaphoran' rereading already opened the question. Frede preserves the Kennedy-tradition reading by silence.

debates.debate_name: Phantasia grafted onto perception vs. pure interpretation

pole_A.claim: Rhetorical phantasia operates at or near the level of direct sensory perception — words 'graft' phantasia onto perception non-metaphorically; vision is more than 'seeing-as-understanding.'

key_evidence.bekker: Rhet. II + III via Nussbaum 1985 modification

pole_B.claim: Phantasia is interpretation — 'abstract thought thought to concrete perceptibles' — scare-quoted 'bringing-before-the-eyes' is seeing-as-understanding (Kennedy 2007).

debates.notes: Hawhee explicitly modifies Nussbaum: Book II 'moves closer to Nussbaum' but adds non-metaphorical grafting onto direct perception.

debates.debate_name: DA III.3 428a1-4 kata metaphoran: standard vs. 'mere show'

pole_A.claim: The bracketed transferred-sense at DA 428a1-4 refers to the broad phainetai-uses (standard editorial reading via Hicks/Ross/Rodier).

pole_B.claim: Nussbaum's rereading: the kata-metaphoran clause references the 'mere show' / ostentation sense — Aristotle is bracketing the colloquial usage to keep the technical noun-account clean.

debates.notes: Aristotle's silence on which transferred sense leaves both defensible; the choice shapes the entire interpretive arc.

pole_A.claim: DA III.11 434a7-10 establishes a robust deliberative phantasia (phantasia bouleutike) doing real cognitive work in practical reasoning, motivating action via single-pictured measure.

pole_B.claim: DA III.11 deliberative passage is marginal or textually unstable; phantasia's primary work is theoretical-cognitive preparation for noein (Ross-tradition / White's confinement to III.3-8).

debates.notes: White's footnote-80 dismissal of practical phantasia is the methodological inverse of Nussbaum's expansion.

pole_A.claim: There is no intellectual memory: memory and dreams are entirely on the sensible side; phantasia is the bridge but remains CONFINED to sensible content. Aristotelian dualism is preserved.

pole_B.claim: Phantasia underwrites a continuous ascent from perception to nous (APo II.19 routed-army; the 'standardized pictures' of DA III.7-8 are intellectually-charged); memory has intellectual purchase via phantasmata.

debates.notes: Frede is the only explicit dualist on this point; others are ambiguous but tend toward continuity.

pole_A.claim: The Thomistic / late-ancient commentary tradition (Themistius, Philoponus, Aquinas's Sentencia) is a legitimate authority for reading DA III's psychology — including the tripartite-phantasia thesis and 'imaginatio' as motion-of-phantasy.

pole_B.claim: The analytic-Anglophone philosophy-of-mind tradition (Schofield, Modrak, Nussbaum, Caston, Wedin, Sorabji) sets the agenda; ancient commentaries function as supplementary evidence but not as governing authorities.

debates.notes: Visible in the citation profiles: Papachristou cites Aquinas heavily; Caston cites Leibniz but not Aquinas.

debates.debate_name: Silent disagreement: citation gaps as engagement-by-omission

pole_A.claim: Major cluster authors are doing serious phantasia work that subsequent authors should engage; silent omission is a meaningful negative judgment (cf. Caston ignores 1985 Nussbaum essay; González skips White/Caston/O'Gorman; Frede uncited by Hawhee; PHX-08 does not engage PHX-04-Caston).

pole_B.claim: Omissions are matters of disciplinary boundary (rhetoric vs. philosophy-of-mind vs. medieval commentary), not silent dismissal; the cluster spans incommensurable subfields where 'should cite' presumes a unity it does not have.

debates.notes: This debate is meta-bibliographic: pole_A treats the cluster as a unified scholarly conversation; pole_B treats it as parallel disciplinary tracks. Generated by Phase 3B synthesis, not present as an explicit tension in any single unit.

debates.debate_name: Phantasia/aisthesis 'one in number, different in being'

pole_A.claim: Two-description / arete-dikaiosune reading: phantasia and aisthesis are ONE activity under TWO descriptions of one power (Nussbaum's preferred parsing).

pole_B.claim: Two-activity / road-up-road-down reading: phantasia is a SECONDARY MOTION arising from the PRIMARY MOTION of aisthesis (White; also Caston via the 'subjunctive causal-powers' analysis).

debates.notes: Both Nussbaum and White concede the textual evidence is mixed; Caston's non-Leibnizian-identity move (fn. 51) is the most theoretically articulated.
